note: Luffy v34 Result a6d93b5c (OPUS-NET-61-13): its review verdicts and its eight free-form model findings.

omissionVerdicts.reason: The cited passages describe rapid movement, which the stationary attack Definition cannot express; no purchase proposal carries that movement or evasion effect.

The cited passage describes a fast, forceful punch that propels its target. Gear 2 adapts speed and force, and knockback is expressible, so the named-technique omission is not justified by the claim that no purchase names it.
omissionVerdicts.action: Add it as a repertoire entry adapted by the relevant purchase, or revise the whole-technique omission.

omissionVerdicts.reason: The supplied passage only identifies it as a Gear 2 version of Stamp and provides no combat effect to adapt safely.

The omission reason relies on naming alone, but the selected source also describes a high-speed double open-palm strike. The record does not establish whether that passage is this named technique, leaving the proposed adaptation connection uncertain.
omissionVerdicts.action: Check the technique passage association and either adapt the described strike or document why it is not the omitted technique.

omissionVerdicts.reason: Its cited central effect is defense and projectile reflection, neither of which the supplied Unit Definition expresses or a purchase proposes.

omissionVerdicts.action: Add it to the repertoire and associate the Gear 3 purchases that adapt it.

omissionVerdicts.reason: The cited passage describes launching and repositioning, which the stationary attack Definition cannot express; no purchase proposes movement.

The cited central effect is enhanced durability, with no corresponding defense mechanic or purchase proposal in the supplied Definition.

omissionVerdicts.action: Add a damage-based headbutt adaptation, or narrow the omission to the unrepresented hardening aspect.

omissionVerdicts.reason: The cited passage describes a hardened fist and apparent ignition. Damage or burn can represent an offensive effect, so the reason that no purchase currently adapts it does not establish that the whole technique cannot be adapted.
omissionVerdicts.action: Add a coherent damage or burn proposal to a purchase, or narrow the omission reason.

omissionVerdicts.reason: The cited passages frame the power claim as possibly joking and do not support a reliable combat effect.
The cited central effect depends on containing shadows and using their combined strength and skills. No typed change or purchase proposal carries those source-dependent behaviors.

thirdPurchaseVerdicts.name: Gigant Pistol
thirdPurchaseVerdicts.reason: 3-x-x adds splash and increased damage while slowing the attack. Its first two purchases only increase damage, and the other paths do not add splash at their third purchase, so it establishes Gear 3’s group-impact identity.

thirdPurchaseVerdicts.name: Jet Pistol
thirdPurchaseVerdicts.reason: x-3-x adds stronger, faster punches after its first two purchases increase only attack rate. The other third purchases specialize in splash or Gear 4 attack speed without the same combined damage and rate change, giving Gear 2 a distinct fast, forceful strike identity.

thirdPurchaseVerdicts.name: Gear 4 Fast Punch
thirdPurchaseVerdicts.reason: x-x-3 adds faster attacks, but x-1-x and x-2-x already increase attack rate, and x-3-x also adds attack rate. It adds no distinguishing capability beyond a dimension already shared by the other paths’ purchases.
thirdPurchaseVerdicts.action: Give the Gear 4 third purchase a distinct supported capability, or revise the path progression.

findings.subject: Omission: Gomu Gomu no Jet Pistol
findings.rule: A whole-technique omission fails when its central effect can be carried by a supported typed change or a coherent proposed mechanic.
findings.message: The cited passage describes Jet Pistol as a fast, forceful punch that propels its target. Gear 2’s attack-rate and damage changes adapt its speed and force, and knockback is an available typed effect, so the reason that it is not named as a separate entry does not justify omitting the technique. Add Jet Pistol to the repertoire or revise the omission to account for its central effect.
findings.action: Add the technique as an adapted repertoire entry or remove it from whole-technique omissions.

findings.subject: Omission: Gomu Gomu no Gigant Pistol
findings.rule: A whole-technique omission fails when a purchase already adapts the technique’s central effect.
findings.message: The cited passage identifies Gigant Pistol as the Gear 3 version of Pistol, and the Gear 3 path adapts enlarged, forceful impact through damage and splash. The claim that the named attack is not separately implemented does not justify omitting its adapted central effect. Add it as a repertoire entry or revise the plan’s coverage.
findings.action: Add Gigant Pistol to the repertoire and associate its adapting purchases.

findings.subject: Omission: Atama Buso
findings.rule: Do not omit a technique as wholly unadaptable when a supported purchase effect can represent its central combat effect.
findings.message: The cited passages describe hardening Luffy’s forehead in preparation for a headbutt. Damage is a supported way to represent a forceful headbutt, so the statement that the evidence does not describe a distinct attack effect does not support omitting the technique wholesale. Add a purchase adaptation or narrow the omission to the unsupported hardening aspect.
findings.action: Add a damage-based headbutt adaptation or revise the omission to name only the unrepresented aspect.

findings.subject: Omission: Gear 2 Buso
findings.rule: A whole-technique omission fails when its central described effect can be represented by a supported effect or proposed mechanic.
findings.message: The cited passage describes a hardened Gear 2 fist and an apparent ignition effect. The omission discusses only the lack of a burn purchase, but a bounded damage or burn proposal could represent those offensive effects. Add the proposed behavior to a purchase or narrow the omission to the unsupported aspect.
findings.action: Add a coherent damage or burn proposal to a purchase, or narrow the omission reason.

findings.subject: x-x-3, Gear 4 Fast Punch
findings.rule: A third purchase must distinguish its path from its own first and second purchases and from the other paths’ purchases.
findings.message: x-x-3 adds faster attack rate, a dimension already developed by x-1-x and x-2-x and by x-3-x. Unlike x-3-x, it adds no other typed change, so the third purchase does not establish a distinct Gear 4 path identity. Give x-x-3 a distinct supported capability or revise the path progression.
findings.action: Give x-x-3 a distinct supported capability beyond faster attacks, or redesign its third-tier role.

findings.subject: x-x-4, Python Pistol
findings.rule: A proposed mechanic must be coherent with its cited technique and must not conflict with the Definition.
findings.message: The proposal says Python redirects the punch after its primary hit, but x-x-4 has no follow-up in its resolved changes. Treating it as an implemented purchase benefit would be false. Either keep redirection explicitly proposed and unresolved at this tier, or add a supported follow-up mechanic to the Definition and purchase.
findings.action: Mark the x-x-4 redirection as a proposal requiring Definition support, or add the typed follow-up support.

findings.subject: 4-x-x, Gigant Pistol Force
findings.rule: A purchase’s effect assessment must agree with its resolved changes.
findings.message: The x-x-4 text lists pierce as an improvement without an effect, but 4-x-x raises pierce from 2 to 3. Correct the plan’s promisesWithoutEffect assessment so it does not deny a delivered benefit.
findings.action: Remove pierce from promisesWithoutEffect for this purchase.

findings.subject: 5-x-x, Gigant Pistol Knockback
findings.rule: A purchase’s effect assessment must agree with its resolved changes.
findings.message: The x-x-5 text lists knockback as an improvement without an effect, but 5-x-x applies knockback. Correct the plan’s promisesWithoutEffect assessment.
findings.action: Remove knockback from promisesWithoutEffect for this purchase.
